summary: In a major expansion of national security space strategy, United States Space Force leaders outlined a blueprint to more than double the service's force size over the next five years, while U.S. Space Command pressed for enhanced orbital domain awareness as the U.S. acknowledged for the first time deploying weapons in space. Defense procurement highlights include the Pentagon and Lockheed Martin agreeing to expand production of the secretive Joint Advanced Tactical Missile, Northrop Grumman being named prime contractor for the Space Force's Ground Moving Target Indicator program, and the U.S. clearing a $24 billion F-35 sale to Saudi Arabia. In civil space and astrophysics, NASA extended the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope mission from 10 to 22 years, awarded launch services for the StarBurst Gamma-Ray Detector, and announced that its Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter spotted a significant new crater on the Moon. Scientific research also advanced as astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope measured extreme gas outflows from distant dead galaxies and discovered the youngest known planet. Commercial space activity saw Viasat and Space42 commit up to $1 billion to their Equatys joint venture, Impulse Space secure $308 million in Series D extension funding, and SEOPS book five launches on Isar Aerospace's Spectrum rocket. Looking ahead, observers should watch for SpaceX's planned first orbital flight of its Starship rocket.
